title: Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming now provides a Linux broadcast SDK
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming now provides a Linux broadcast SDK
body_markdown:
The Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) Linux broadcast SDK is now available for IVS Real-Time Streaming. Applications running on Linux can join an IVS stage, receive audio from participants, and send audio back to the stage in real time. The SDK provides a C API and Go language bindings.


The Linux broadcast SDK is ideal for AI applications that enrich live streams by processing audio, such as transcription, translation, and content moderation, as well as voice agents that converse with participants.


[Amazon IVS](https://aws.amazon.com/ivs/) is a managed live streaming solution designed to make low-latency or real-time video available to viewers around the world. Visit the[AWS Region table](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regional-product-services/) for a full list of AWS Regions where the Amazon IVS console and APIs for control and creation of video streams are available.


To learn more, see[IVS Broadcast SDK: Linux Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ivs/latest/RealTimeUserGuide/broadcast-linux.html) .
